text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 10 in history:
1512 - James V of Scotland, who allied his country with France against the English, was born. He became king at the age of 17 months.
1755 - Christian Friedrich Samuel Hahnemann, German physician who pioneered homeopathic medicine, born.
1778 - William Hazlitt, English writer, essayist, philosopher and critic, born.
1827 - Lewis Wallace, U.S. novelist, soldier, diplomat and lawyer, born. Best known for "Ben Hur".
1829 - William Booth, founder of the Salvation Army, born. In 1865 he started "The Christian Mission" in London's East End, which in 1878 became the Salvation Army.
1847 - Joseph Pulitzer, U.S. newspaper owner who instituted the Pulitzer Prize, born.
1864 - Archduke Maximilian of Austria accepted the throne of Mexico.
1868 - George Arliss, British actor of stage and screen, born. He was famous for his portrayal of Disraeli, Voltaire, Richelieu and Wellington.
1919 - Revolutionary leader Emiliano Zapata was ambushed and killed by government troops in Mexico.
1921 - Dr Sun Yat-sen was elected president of China.
1922 - The Genoa Conference opened to discuss the reconstruction of Europe after World War One.
1929 - Max von Sydow, Swedish actor, born; he starred in the Ingmar Bergman films "The Seventh Seal", "Through A Glass Darkly" and "Shame".
1932 - In Germany, Paul von Hindenburg received 19 million votes in the presidential elections beating Adolf Hitler's 13 million votes.
1932 - Actor Omar Sharif was born in Egypt as Michael Shalhoub; he played the popular romantic leads in such films as "Lawrence of Arabia" and "Doctor Zhivago".
1944 - Russian troops recaptured Odessa from the Germans in World War Two.
1944 - A British midget submarine secretly entered Bergen harbour in Norway and sunk the German merchant ship Barenfels.

1954 - Pioneering French film director Auguste Lumiere died. Together with his brother Louis Jean he was responsible for many early inventions in cinema history, including making what is considered to be the first film, "La Sortie des usines Lumiere".
1962 - Film director Michael Curtiz died; born in Hungary as Mihali Kertesz, he won an Oscar for "Casablanca".
1963 - The U.S. submarine Thresher sank off Cape Cod in the Atlantic with the loss of 129 lives.
1966 - Evelyn Waugh, English novelist, died. Remembered for novels such as "Scoop", "The Loved One", and "Brideshead Revisited".
1972 - An earthquake struck southern Iran, killing more than 5,000 people.
1972 - More than 50 countries signed a treaty outlawing the stockpiling of biological weapons.
1973 - In Switzerland, 108 people died when a plane crashed while attempting to land at Basel.
1974 - Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir resigned over differences within her Labour Party.
1980 - Spain and Britain agreed to reopen the border between Gibraltar and Spain, closed in 1969.
1983 - President Reagan's Middle East peace plan collapsed when King Hussein of Jordan failed to reach agreement with the PLO on the terms of the deal.
1990 - Three European hostages kidnapped at sea in 1987 by Palestinian extremists headed by Abu Nidal were released in Beirut and handed to the French embassy.
1992 - A huge IRA bomb exploded in London's financial district; three people were killed and 91 injured.
1994 - NATO warplanes launched air strikes for the first time on Serb forces advancing on the Bosnian Moslem town of Gorazde, a U.N.-declared "safe area".
1994 - Argentines approved a reform allowing President Carlos Menem to run for a second term.
1995 - Veteran revolutionary Chen Yun, one of China's leading economic planners, died at 90.
1996 - Chinese Premier Li Peng's visit to France was marred by a diplomatic wrangle with his French counterpart Alain Juppe over human rights in Beijing.
